title: infra_findings
description: Findings-record output document emitted by review agents (specdev-reviewer) and consumed by fix agents (specdev-impl). One document represents the merged findings of a single review round for a single scope. The dedup key for individual findings is the tuple (kind, location, signature). See Proposal K §4.1 (taxonomy), §5.4 (schema-only — no CLI), and §11.7 (path resolution).

$schema.description: The schema this document conforms to. Required by `specdev validate` (E520 without it); optional here so that a plain JSON Schema check also accepts the file the review loop merges.

round.description: 1+ (the schema has no cap; a run of `specdev loop` stops at its `--cap`, default 5). Increments per review-fix iteration.

scope.description: Short identifier of the review scope. Examples: 'step-04', 'steps-04-05-cross', 'ms-batch-1-plan', or a plan-item id as the plan schema spells it ('PWRESET_CONFIRM_EXPIRED_01'). Lowercase letters, digits, '_' and '-', or uppercase letters, digits and '_' (no mixing). In a run of `specdev loop` the brief gives the value and the tool refuses a file with another one; the files of a run are in its folder (.specdev/runs/<run-id>/), and a code run also writes 'findings_<group_id>_<n>.json' or 'findings_<batch>_review_<n>.json' under .specdev/findings/ for `specdev milestone-state`.

generated_at.description: Unix-epoch seconds (integer) when this document was emitted. Used for run correlation; not a uniqueness key.

coverage.description: What the reviewer was given and what it read, for a file handed to `specdev loop`: `assigned` and `read` hold node ids and contract paths, `not_run` what it could not read. `specdev loop next` refuses a file whose `read` lacks an assigned entry or whose `not_run` is not empty. Optional: a file that is not handed to `specdev loop` may omit it.

judgements.description: The reviewer's verdict on each finding of an earlier round that `specdev loop` asked it to judge: `resolved` or `not_resolved` for a fix (or an accepted link), `decline_right` or `finding_right` for a decline. `key` is the finding's key as the brief gives it; `quote` is the text that shows the verdict.

findings.description: Array of finding-records emitted by the reviewer(s). May be empty (zero findings is the CONVERGED predicate per §4.1).

finding.description: One finding-record. Dedup key across reviewers within a round is the tuple (kind, location, signature). Severity follows the P0/P1/P2 priority language used elsewhere in the toolkit.

kind.description: Taxonomy bucket (Proposal K §4.1). 'gap' = required content missing; 'miss' = incomplete upstream coverage; 'bug' = factually wrong against schema/upstream/canon; 'regression' = downstream broken by upstream change; 'assumption' = un-grounded inference; 'ambiguity' = multiple valid readings or precedence conflict; 'hallucination' = invented ID/enum/command/path/canon-ref; 'drift' = artifact-vs-reality or artifact-vs-artifact divergence; 'coverage' = trace/fixture/NFR mapping incomplete; 'determinism' = non-reproducible decision, racy invariant, free-text where enum expected; 'seed-grounding' = artifact ignores or contradicts seed content the step is required to ingest (per spec/common/seed_manifest.json step_requirements[NN]; global_seed_order governs read order only).

location.description: Where the finding sits: the id of the node it is about, with '#<field>' for one field of it (e.g. 'fr-password-reset#statement'); a finding about no node holds a file path, a JSON pointer or 'file#pointer'; a code-phase finding holds '<file>#<function or class>' (e.g. 'src/routes/confirm.ts#confirmPasswordReset'), no line number. A string, not a pattern.

signature.description: The key of the finding. In a run of `specdev loop` the tool sets it to '<kind>|<location>' when it takes the file in, whatever the reviewer wrote, and merges the findings of a round by it; a file written by hand holds any stable string.

message.description: Human-readable description of the finding. Should be specific enough to drive a fix; should be normalized (stable wording for the same underlying issue) so that signature dedup works across reviewers.

severity.description: Severity by impact, not by kind. P0 = a defect: someone who builds from the text as written builds the wrong thing or cannot build. P1 = a defect that leaves the builder or a later step to guess. P2 = wording or preference: the spec would say the same and the build would be the same. `specdev loop` does not converge while a P0 or P1 is open; a P2 is a note of the report. There is no P3: what is not worth a P2 is not reported.

evidence.description: Optional citation(s) supporting the finding. Array of strings (e.g. quoted source lines, command output excerpts). Reviewer agents are encouraged to populate this so the fix agent can ground the edit.

evidence_quotes.description: Quotes that `specdev loop` checks: `text` must occur in `source` (a node id, or a file path from the host root or the toolkit root), whitespace apart. A finding handed to `specdev loop` with no quote, or with a quote that does not occur, is refused and listed in the run's `rejected.json`. For something missing, quote the contract, seed or upstream node that requires it.

suggested_fix.description: Optional reviewer-proposed remediation (free text). The fix agent treats this as advisory, not authoritative.

catalog_tag.description: Audit catalog item (D1-D14 for drift, I1-I13 for invariant) that this finding violates. Optional in the schema; the devspec_pr_audit skill requires it to be populated for every audit finding. K §4.1 callers may omit it.

status.description: Finding lifecycle state. open = active, deferred = acknowledged but not in current Part B, verified = fixed and confirmed. The devspec_pr_audit skill is responsible for defaulting absent values to 'open' — validators do not fill this in.

upstream_refs.description: Optional array of upstream references this finding ties back to — canonical IDs (e.g. 'cn:project:term-foo'), FR IDs (e.g. 'fr-user-login'), capability IDs, or other stable identifiers. Drives 'miss' / 'coverage' / 'assumption' findings into the upstream-backlog view.

origin.description: Where the defect came from. 'introduced-on-branch' = the text was changed on this branch; 'pre-existing-on-main' = already present at the base ref; 'stale-after-fix' = left behind or made wrong by a fix of this loop. Optional. A finding of kind 'regression' (a downstream artifact broken by an upstream change) is never 'introduced-on-branch': text changed against the base is a 'bug' or a 'drift' with this origin.
